summary: Sekigahara is a lean two-player card-driven wargame about maneuvering armies across feudal Japan, where hidden unit strength and clever hand management matter more than dice luck. Battles are resolved through card play rather than randomness, so the tension comes from bluffing troop strength and committing forces at the right crossroads.
praised: elegant, low-luck battle resolution using cards instead of dice
tight two-player design with real strategic depth
quick to learn for a wargame
criticised: can feel abstract or dry for players wanting miniatures-style combat
map and iconography take a session to fully internalize
steep skill gap between experienced and new players

interaction.kind: direct military conflict and blocking over shared provinces/roads
interaction.detail: With only two players and no private board at all, literally every action — moving armies, contesting a province, cutting a supply route, committing units to battle — is aimed at what the other side is doing. The entire map is one contested shared space.
interaction.said: Sekigahara is talked about as a tense, elegant two-player wargame where 'every move is a threat', praised for how tightly the two sides are forced to fight over the same handful of provinces and supply lines.

subsystems: territorial control (political points from castles and resource locations)
scoring.how_you_win: You win instantly if you kill the enemy leader (or, as Tokugawa, capture Hideyori); if neither leader falls, the game ends after week 7 and whoever controls more political points — castles at 2 each, resource locations at 1 each — wins.
scoring.score_note: won by control/attrition, not a tallied score

theme.said: frequently praised as a masterclass in theme-through-mechanism — 'the units flip and defect exactly like the real clans did', 'you feel the fragile, improvised alliance system of the actual campaign'
theme.why: hidden units that flip loyalty when captured or bribed, and daimyo blocks that must be pried away from an opponent's control rather than simply destroyed, model the real historical uncertainty over which clans would actually fight for whom at Sekigahara

style.why: Two players wage direct territorial war for control of Japan, but combat is resolved deterministically by played card values rather than dice, keeping randomness low.
